values.value: You have just told us the estate reaches well outside Marketing Cloud. Who actually MASTERS consent — the CRM, a CDP, a preference service — and is that system in scope for this migration or somebody else's roadmap?

[{"value":1,"label":"Nobody is sure. Consent state exists in more than one system and they are known to disagree.","points":1},{"value":2,"label":"Another team's system masters it, it is out of scope for this programme, and no one from that team has been in these conversations.","points":1},{"value":3,"label":"Another system masters it, the owner is named and engaged, and the interface is documented.","points":3},{"value":4,"label":"A single system masters consent, it is in scope, and the migration can re-point to it without renegotiating ownership.","points":4}]
Get a name, not a system. 'Who do we call when a customer disputes a consent record' is the question that produces one.

skills/mce-mcn-helper/references/skills/10-roadmap.md — the external-dependency section, where an adjacent workstream with no named owner is the standard cause of a slipped phase, applied to the one workstream that cannot be descoped for legal reasons. docs/runbooks/assessment-instrument.md — the layer-3 test (same position, same risk theme, different KIND of question) and the branching rules this row is the worked example of. NON-LINEAR POINTS, DELIBERATELY. Options 1 and 2 are both worth 1. "The systems disagree" and "another team owns it and has never been in the room" are not one step apart in remediation cost — they are the same problem, discovered at different times, and both mean a consent reconciliation workstream before any send. Making the second worth 2 would have said something the estate does not support. The slot still bottoms at 1 and tops at 4, so the pair is still scored out of 32 and still banded at 14/20/26: points bought a shape, not a different maximum.
